3. On the death of the said Badsha Miah, the suit property along with other land devolved upon the plaintiff-respondent by way of inheritance. In the year 1958-1959 the suit property along with other properties was requisitioned by the Government, defendant-proforma-respondent No.15 for the purpose of rehabilitation of Mohajaria from India as well as for the purpose of constructing a Road, namely "The Ring Road" to protect the Nuclear Houses from flood in LA Case No.30 of 1958-1959. The plaintiff-respondents did not draw any compensation money for the suit land with the hope that the same would be given back to them by the Government as they did not have any piece of land in the Dhaka City. 

 4. The Nuclear House for rehabilitation of the Muhajirs and the ring road for which the suit land along with other lands of the plaintiffs was requisitioned have already been completed as per plan of the Government and the Ring road has also been constructed to the north of the Nuclear Houses and beyond the Ring Road the suit lands are lying to the adjacent North of the Ring road and the suit land and, as such, are not utilized for the purpose for which the same was requisitioned. It is stated that the plaintiffs did neither take compensation for the suit land nor they have accepted two plots measuring 13/4 katha each allotted to them in the planned area as those could not meet their requirements. 

 5. The plaintiffs came to know that the suit property was leased out to defendant No.3. The present petitioner, who, as per the plaintiff, was threatening the plaintiffs with dispossession, had been impleaded as defendant No.3 in the suit for proper adjudication of the matter in his presence. The plaintiffs made a representation to the officials of the Governments requesting them to derequisition of the suit land in their favour without any loss of time in the months of August, 1983 but unlike other occasions instead of giving any assurance to that effect they refused the request of the plaintiffs and hence they were constrained to bring the suit. 

 10. The Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh being the 16 annas exclusive owner and possessor of the scheduled property of the plaint through acquisition under LA Case No. 30 of 1958-59 defendant No.2, the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka allotted a plot measuring 0.71 acre out of the scheduled property to the Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) in the year 1975, as required for Nursery/Horticulture and open sale centre in the greater interest of the citizens of the Dhaka Metropolitan City. Accordingly, the BADC took possession of the said plot of land and started Nursery and sale centre thereon in the year 1975. 

 11. Thereafter, the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Works, leased out the said 0.71 acre of land out of the scheduled property of the plaint, to the allottee/tenant Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation (BADC) by a registered lease agreement dated 23-12-1981 for a period of 99 (ninety nine) years at a premium of Taka 3,75,915 (Taka three lacs seventy five thousand nine hundred and fifteen only) paid by the tenant BADC vide treasury challan No.28 KA dated 03-7-1981. 

 13. At one stage a portion of the said leased property was forcibly occupied by some bad elements of the locality and the BADC as a legal owner of the said property ousted those bad elements from the land through police force. Accordingly the BADC has been enjoying the leased property peacefully, without interference from any corner. Afterwards, while the BADC was in possession of the leased property being 0.71 acres out of the scheduled property of the plaint as aforesaid, the plaintiffs filed the present suit being TS No.290 of 1984 in the 1st Court of the Munsif at Dhaka praying for derequisition and khas possession of the scheduled land property including the said 0.71 acres of leased property rightfully owned and possessed by the BADC. The Chairman of the BADC has been impleaded in the suit as defendant No.3 but the Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation itself and other concerned officers including the Secretary of the Corporation who has entered into the aforesaid 99 years lease agreement with the government have not been impleaded as defendants in the instant suit. 

 19. Mr A.M. Aminuddin, learned Attorney-General, appearing on behalf of the appellant, submits that section 14A of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948, itself bars filing a suit in a civil court questioning legality of the order passed or any action taken under this Act and thus, the decree passed by the Courts below is a nullity and the High Court Division committed an error of law in maintaining the decree for derequisition. He further submits that in view of section 5(7) of the (Emergency) Requisition Property Act, 1948, the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh is the owner and possessor of the said quantum of land acquired in LA Case No.30 of 1958-1959 out of which 0.71 acre of land was allotted to the appellant by way of lease agreement in the year 1975 as required for nursery and opening a sale center in the greater interest of the citizens of the Dhaka Metropolitan City. He then submits that there is no scope to say that the suit land is unused and unutilized and the appellant is not the requiring body, and it has been done without jurisdiction. Therefore, the High Court Division committed error of law in affirming the concurrent judgments of the Courts below. He continues to submit that the burden of proof lies upon the plaintiffs to prove the case as alleged and the question of non-service of notices under sections 5(A), 5(C) and 7 of the said Act and non-receiving the compensation money incorporated in the plaint by way of amendment long after 12 years of filing the suit are required to be proved by the plaintiffs which they have utterly failed and, as such, the High Court Division committed an error of law in failing to consider that the amendment was made after a long lapse of time incorporating of those facts with a view to simply making out a case and those facts, as it appears has not been proved. 

 20. Mr Probir Neogi, learned Senior Advocate, appearing on behalf of respondent Nos.1-8, on the other hand, submits that the ex pane decree passed by the trial Court has been affirmed by the appellate Court and the High Court Division and that there is no scope for interference as the appellant failed to prove his case as it was not present before the trial Court by filing written statement and also by adducing evidence and, as such, no interference is called for. He further submits that the scheme for the purpose of rehabilitation of the refugees/ Muhajirs from India and for the purpose of construction of Ring-Road to save and protect the Nuclear House from flood had been fully materialized and while the Ring-Road had been constructed the suit property was not used for the purpose for which it was acquisitioned and the suit property remains unutilized and, as such, the suit was rightly decreed by the trial Court which was upheld up to the High Court Division. He further submits that section I4A of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948 mandates no absolute bar in entertainment of a suit by a civil Court and jurisdiction, even if excluded, civil Court has got jurisdiction to examine whether the Statutory Tribunal has acted in conformity with the Fundamental Principles of Requisition and Acquisition and civil Court rightly and legally entertained the suit and judicial verdicts handed down by Courts below had been very rightly maintained and upheld by the High Court Division and no interference is called for by this Division. He also submits that it is admitted by defendant-appellant that the suit property along with other properties had been requisitioned for the purpose of rehabilitation of Refugees/ Mohajirs from India and also for the purpose of construction of Ring-Road to save and protect Nuclear Houses from flood and scheme of requisition for the purpose of rehabilitation of Refugees/Mohajirs from India and also for the purpose of constitution Ring-Road to save and protect the Nuclear Houses from flood had been fully materialized and satisfied and the suit property was not at all used for the purpose of requisition and the suit property remained unused and unutilized. Admittedly, 0.71 acres of land out of the suit property had been leased out to the defendant-appellant though the defendant-appellant as requiring body did not pray for leasing out 0.71 acre of land and, as such, no interference is called for. He lastly submits that the unutilized land is in exclusive possession of the plaintiff-respondents and the only thing Government is required to do is to release/ derequisition 0.71 acre of land in favour of the plaintiff-respondents. 

 "That section 14A of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act, 1948, itself bars filing a suit in a civil court questioning legality of the order passed or any action taken under this Act and thus, the decree passed by the Courts below is a nullity and the High Court Division committed an error of law in maintaining the decree for derequisition; that the view of section 5(7) of the (Emergency) Requisition of Property Act,1948 the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh was the owner and possessor of the said quantum of land and out of which 0.71 acre of land was allotted to the petitioner by way of lease agreement in the year 1975 as required for nursery and opening sale center in the greater interest of the citizens of the Dhaka Metropolitan City and in such circumstances it cannot be said that the land is unused and unutilized and the petitioner is not the requiring body, and it has been done without jurisdiction; that the settled principle of law that the burden of proof lies upon the plaintiffs to prove the case as being alleged and the question of non-service of notice under sections 5(A), 5(C) and 7 of the said Act, 1948 and non-receiving the compensation money incorporate in the plaint by way of amendment long after 12 years of filing the suit and the High Court Division committed an error of law in failing to consider that the amendment was made after a long passage of time incorporating of those facts with a view to simply make out a case and those facts, as it appears has not been proved." 

 23. It had been admitted by both the parties that the suit property along with other properties was requisitioned and acquisitioned in LA Case No.30 of 1958-1959 for the purpose of rehabilitation of Refugees/Mohajirs from India and also for the purpose of construction of Ring-Road to save and protect the Nuclear Houses from flood. It is also admitted that after conclusion of rehabilitation programme of the Refugees/Mohajirs and also after construction of Ring-Road, the suit property remains unused. The plaintiffs contended that keeping unused acquired suit property by the government was illegal and the plaintiffs were entitled to get back the suit property on derequisition. The plaintiffs also contended that the lease deed dated 23-1-1981 executed and registered in favour of defendant No.3 appellant by defendant Nos.1 and 2 was illegal and defendant No.3 appellant on the strength of that lease deed did not acquire any right, title and interest in the suit land. 

 25. In support of its aforesaid finding, the High Court Division relied upon the case of The Federation of Pakistan through the Secretary, Establishement Division, Government of Pakistan Rawalpindi vs Saeed Ahmad Khan, PLD 1974 (SC) 151. In the decision referred to above Hamdur Rahman, CJ held that a malafide act and coram non judice stand on the same footing and no ouster clause in any enactment howsoever widely coached can save them from judicial scrutiny. 

 26. Having gone through the decision cited above, we find that it has no manner of application in the case in hand. Admittedly, the plaintiff obtained ex parte decree from the trial Court on 21-9-1999. We have also gone through the judgment delivered by the trial Court and the trial Court did not at all come to the finding that the acquisition proceedings under LA Case No.30 of 1958-1959 was a malafide one. 

 29. Therefore, the finding of the High Court Division that the appellant resorted to a malafide way while acquiring the suit property and other properties under LA Case No.30 of 1958-1959 does not hold good. The High Court Division also came to the finding that defendant No.2, Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka, did not serve any notice under sections 5(3), 5A and 7 of the Act. But having gone through the judgment, we find that the trial Court did not come to a finding that notices under sections 5(3), 5A and 7 of the Act were not served upon the plaintiffs. Mere assertion made in the plaint without producing the relevant documents cannot prove that notices under the aforesaid sections were not served upon the plaintiff. Admittedly, the gazette notification under section 5(7) of the Act was published in the official Gazette on 25-6-1973. Section 5(7) runs as follows: 

 "5(7). The Government shall then publish in the Official Gazette a notice to the effect that the Government has decided to acquire the requisitioned property. On and from the beginning of the day on which the notice is so published the requisitioned property shall vest absolutely in the Government free from all encumbrances and the period of such requisition of such property shall end. 

 30. According to section 5(7) of the Act as soon as gazette notification is published the requisitioned property vests absolutely in the Government free from all encumbrances and the period of such acquisition of such property shall end. 

 33. What is remarkable to note here is that this amendment of plaint was filed after lapse of 10 years of institution of the suit and that the trial Court accepted the amendment after long lapse of time. Admittedly, as soon as gazette notification has been published in the official gazette, the acquired property including the suit property vested in the Government free from all encumbrances and the Government is at liberty to use the property for any other purpose and the original owners lost their right over the acquired land for good. Admittedly, the suit property along with other properties was acquired in LA Case No.30 of 1958-1959 and the gazette notification in respect thereof was published in the official gazette on 25-6-1973. Therefore, the suit itself was not maintainable from its very inception. The plaintiff cannot take the plea that the suit is maintainable because of malafide. 

 35. The High Court Division came to the finding that refusal to derequisition of unused and unutilized property in favour of plaintiff-respondent Nos.1-8 appears to be malafide on the part of defendant Nos. I and 2. Admittedly, gazette notification has been published in respect of the suit property along with other properties on 25-6-1973 prior to filing of the suit. According to the spirit of section 5(7) of the Act, the properties so acquired shall vest in the Government free from all encumbrances. Therefore, the Government is at liberty to lease it out to anybody whomever it likes. 

 36. Over and above, the property acquired for one public purpose may be used for another public purpose since the property under acquisition vest in the Government free from all encumbrances. In this connection, reliance may be placed on the case of Brahamanbaria Pourashava vs Secretary, Ministry of Land Reforms, Government of Bangladesh, 51 DLR (AD) 84 wherein it has been held that there is no principle of law under which once a property has been validly acquired for a public purpose, as admitted by the Government and has been vested in the requiring body then even if the said property be utilized for a different purpose, the acquisition shall not stand void. 

 37. Therefore, it appears that plaintiff-respondent Nos.l-8 cannot claim the acquired property once it has been validly acquired. Admittedly, the suit property has been leased out to Bangladesh Agricultural Development Corporation in 1975 for nursery/horticulture and sale centre for the greater interest of the citizens of the Dhaka Metropolitan City. The lease deed has been registered on 23-12-1981 for a period of 99 years. The plaintiffs filed Title Suit No.290 of 1984 in the First Court of the then Munsif Court, Dhaka after registration of the lease deed in favour of the appellants. The unused suit property was also utilized for public purpose and the Government is at liberty to do so since the disputed property and other properties vested in it pursuant to the gazette notification dated 26-6-1973 in LA Case No.30 of 1958-1959.
